Write a robot model as URDF

Source: R/urdf.R
robot_write_urdf.Rd

Exports links (inertial parameters and geometry), joints and limits. URDF has no joint offset or post-motion transform, so the export keeps the kinematics exact by folding an offset into the joint origin and by splitting a joint with a post transform into the moving joint, a massless intermediate link named <child>_motion, and a fixed joint named <joint>_post (a numeric suffix is added if a name is taken). The extra joints can change the breadth-first order of the movable joints; when the reimported configuration order differs, a warning gives both orders. Names are XML-escaped.

Usage

robot_write_urdf(robot, file = NULL, fill_limits = NULL)

Arguments

robot

A robot_model.

file

Output path, or NULL to return the XML string.

fill_limits

NULL (the default) to require every revolute and prismatic joint to carry effort and velocity limits, or c(effort = , velocity = ) giving the values written for joints that leave them unspecified. These values are read back literally.

Value

The URDF text, invisibly when written to a file.

Details

Limits keep their literal meaning: URDF requires effort and velocity on every revolute and prismatic joint, and a value of 0 forbids motion for every URDF reader. When a joint leaves them unspecified (NULL), the export stops unless fill_limits supplies the values to write. Joint damping and friction are written as a <dynamics> element, although the dynamics functions do not apply them. Forward kinematics of every original frame is preserved; the exported model has extra frames. Convex-hull geometry has no URDF equivalent and is omitted with a warning.

Examples

robot <- robot_example("planar2")
txt <- robot_write_urdf(robot, fill_limits = c(effort = 50, velocity = 5))
back <- robot_read_urdf(txt)
pose_translation(robot_fk(back, c(pi / 2, pi / 2), "link2"))
#> [1] -1  1  0
